description:
File: pkix-path-builder/Cargo.toml:11

The crate lists 'no-std' in its categories, which on crates.io signals that it works in bare-metal/no_std environments. However, pkix-path-builder unconditionally uses alloc (line 31 of src/lib.rs: extern crate alloc) and requires Vec<Certificate> allocations throughout.

The crate works only with no_std + alloc (not no_std without alloc). The crates.io 'no-std' category typically implies alloc is available (it's a common convention), but this is not universally understood. The crate description, README, and doc comment don't mention the alloc requirement.

Fix: Add a note in the crate-level doc comment (lib.rs) that no_std support requires the alloc crate, e.g.: '# no_std

This crate is no_std-compatible when the alloc crate is available.' This follows the pattern used by many alloc-dependent no_std crates.
title: pkix-path-builder Cargo.toml lists no-std category but does not document alloc requirement
